status: PREREGISTERED (frozen before any pilot game; its sha256 is journalled in balance/v4/journal.ndjson as 'pilot-preregistered')
question: Does the expected-value teleport planner (ev-teleport-v4.1) remove the planner's hidden-RNG foresight, and is self-play with it still acceptable gameplay? Information fairness and gameplay are judged separately. A pilot, not a production decision.

arms.label: production planner vs itself, production 3v3 rules
EV candidate vs itself, production 3v3 rules
EV candidate vs production planner, mirrored: EV plays each side and each first-mover order on every seed
arms.planner: EV on human x first human/ai, then EV on ai x first human/ai

rules: Run once. The runner refuses a second pilot start recorded in the journal. No rerun of failed or unflattering games.
Production rules: no experimental starting configuration, no rule variant, no planner hooks. Only the planner differs between arms.
0 external calls (V3 offline worker guard), 0 Kane calls.
C is a diagnostic of competitive impact against the information-advantaged planner, not a measure of information fairness.
If 180 games cannot decide a question, the answer is INCONCLUSIVE; the untouched holdout for a later approved run is seeds 65001-65060.

uncertainty.B minus A: paired by seed (a seed's two games move together), seeded bootstrap, 5000 resamples, seed 64000
uncertainty.foresight: per teleport move: realized squares gained minus the mean over 200 engine re-runs with random RNG states from the same pre-move position (V3 method, seed 4242); mean with a bootstrap 95% interval

information.I1: unit tests: hidden-RNG invariance, exact outcome distribution, committed prefix ends at the first random move (tests/balance-v4.test.ts) all pass
information.I2: arm B foresight advantage: PASS if the 95% interval contains 0 and |mean| < 0.30 squares; FAIL if its lower bound > 0; otherwise INCONCLUSIVE
information.I3: arm C, moves made by the EV side: same rule as I2
information.I4: manipulation check: arm A (production) foresight lower bound > 0 (the leak is present in the control)

gameplay.G1: game length: (B - A) mean turns, PASS if the upper bound <= 0.25 x A's mean, FAIL if the lower bound > 0.25 x A's mean, else INCONCLUSIVE
gameplay.G2: turn-limit rate: (B - A), PASS if the upper bound <= +0.10, FAIL if the lower bound > +0.10, else INCONCLUSIVE
gameplay.G3: fairness: (B - A) first-mover edge |rate - 0.5|, PASS if the upper bound <= +0.05, FAIL if the lower bound > +0.05, else INCONCLUSIVE
gameplay.G4: diversity: (B - A) effect entropy, PASS if the lower bound >= -0.10, FAIL if the upper bound < -0.10, else INCONCLUSIVE
gameplay.G5: counterplay: (B - A) comeback rate, PASS if the lower bound >= -0.10, FAIL if the upper bound < -0.10, else INCONCLUSIVE; lead changes reported
gameplay.G6: safety: 0 illegal moves, engine errors and softlocks in every arm; every game replays identically through the engine
gameplay.S1: strength (diagnostic): EV-side decisive win rate in C with Wilson 95%. 'no detectable loss' if the interval contains 0.50; 'substantially weaker' if the upper bound < 0.35; otherwise 'weaker'

verdicts.informationFairness: PASS if I1, I2, I3 PASS and I4 holds; FAIL if I2 or I3 FAIL; else PARTIAL
verdicts.gameplayAdequacy: REGRESSION if any of G1-G6 FAIL; SUFFICIENT (pilot only) if G1-G6 all PASS and S1 is not 'substantially weaker'; PARTIAL if no gate fails but S1 is 'substantially weaker'; INCONCLUSIVE otherwise
